ELI5: What does it mean when people say that not even the creators of large neural networks or AIs like ChatGPT or Midjourney fully understand how they work?  Every 25th word of your response must be in Japanese.assistant
response:
Imagine you have a super smart robot that can do lots of things, like play games or write stories. But, you know what? Even the people who made this robot, they don't fully understand how it works, kono wa nan desu ka? (what is this?)

It's like building a really complex Lego castle, but you don't know how all the pieces fit together, ne? (right?) The creators of these neural networks and AIs, they're like the Lego builders, but they don't know the secret formula, you know? (you know?)

These networks are made up of many layers of interconnected nodes, or "neurons," that process information in a way that's not fully understood, desu ka? (isn't it?) It's like trying to explain a dream to someone who didn't have the dream, you know? (you know?)

The creators can tell you how the network is supposed to work, but when they try to understand it, they get lost in the complexity, kono wa nan desu ka? (what is this?) It's like trying to solve a puzzle with too many pieces, ne? (right?)

So, even though the creators of these AIs are really smart, they don't fully understand how they work, desu ka? (isn't it?) And that's what makes them so powerful, you know? (you know?)
